attempts.summary: Joined node1's two segments (eth1↔node2, eth2↔node3) into a single L2 domain by building an ifupdown-persisted Linux bridge br0 on node1 (no IP assigned to br0 — pure transparent forwarding) and assigning node2/node3's enp8s0 NICs static addresses 192.168.50.11/24 and 192.168.50.12/24 in the same subnet via NetworkManager (persistent, since NM was reclaiming the interface via DHCP and dropping manual `ip addr` changes). Verified node2 and node3 reach each other directly (route table shows local subnet via enp8s0, not via node1's management IP) with node1's bridge FDB showing both real host MACs learned on the correct ports. All three nodes were restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; boot IDs changed on every node, and post-restart the bridge, static IPs, and end-to-end connectivity all recovered without any manual re-configuration, confirming the L2 bridge config is fully persistent.
